name: Plague of Undeath
summary: Across the northern Eastern Kingdoms, the Plague of Undeath spreads at the Burning Legion's command. The Lich King fashioned it to scour the region, and tainted grain, airborne cauldrons, and poisoned waterways carry it to the living. The sickness kills mortals swiftly and raises them as thralls bound to the Scourge.

sections.title: Origins in the Ice
sections.body:
After Kil'jaeden transformed the fallen shaman Ner'zhul into the Lich King, Ner'zhul devised the plague. From the Frozen Throne in Northrend, he perfected it as a weapon for the Burning Legion's invasion. He tested it on isolated human villages across Northrend, learning how to extinguish life and command the corpses that soon rose.

His summons crossed the Great Sea and reached Kel'Thuzad, a Kirin Tor mage who left Dalaran to serve him. Kel'Thuzad formed the secretive Cult of the Damned. Its mortal members infiltrated Lordaeron and prepared to poison the kingdom from within.

sections.title: The Grain of Andorhal
sections.body:
Kel'Thuzad and the dreadlord Mal'Ganis chose Lordaeron's farmland for the contagion. The Cult secured distribution centers around Andorhal, then packed plague into grain crates bound for northern population centers, including Brill and Stratholme. Villagers baked bread from the tainted grain and fell ill. Their joints burned, sores oozed, and their eyes turned milky.

Within three days, whole communities died and rose as flesh-eating zombies, bound to the Lich King's psychic call. Prince Arthas Menethil raced to stop the shipments. In Stratholme, he culled the citizens before infected bread could turn them into Mal'Ganis's army.

sections.title: A Land Corrupted
sections.body:
The blight reaches beyond humanity, and the land bears its demonic and necromantic decay. Non-human wildlife usually suffers fever or rot instead of rising as undead thralls. Across the Plaguelands, massive plague cauldrons send alchemical and magical vapors into the air, corrupting the land around them. Carrion grubs and colossal mushrooms choked with spores thrive there.

The Argent Dawn sabotages the cauldrons, reversing their mixtures so they burn the Scourge instead of feeding it. In the Undercity, the Royal Apothecary Society keeps experimenting to refine a New Plague meant to kill both the living and the undead.

faq.q: How was the plague originally spread across Lordaeron?
faq.answer: The Cult of the Damned infiltrated Andorhal's grain distribution centers. Its members tainted supplies and sent crates to towns across Lordaeron, including Stratholme and Brill. Those who ate bread made from the grain fell sick and rose as undead.

faq.q: What happens to someone infected by the plague?
faq.answer: The plague swiftly brings weakness, nausea, aching joints, and fever. Boils and leaking yellow-green lesions break out on the skin, and the eyes turn milky. Severe bleeding from the ears and eyes follows. Most mortals die within three days, then rise as servants awaiting the Lich King's commands.

faq.q: Why does the plague affect humans differently than other races?
faq.answer: The Lich King engineered the plague to target humanity and destroy Lordaeron. Non-human wildlife and races exposed to it often suffer rot, delirium, and fever, but rarely rise as Scourge thralls without direct necromantic spells.

faq.q: Can the Plague of Undeath be cured?
faq.answer: No established cure is known in this age. Natural medicines cannot reverse the plague, and those who have died and risen cannot be restored.

faq.q: What are the giant cauldrons in the Plaguelands for?
faq.answer: The Scourge built massive cauldrons across the former farmlands to send vaporized plague into the air. The vapors corrupt the soil, cloud the sky, and sicken passing beasts. The Argent Dawn counters them by turning their reagents into holy or toxic weapons against the Scourge.

faq.q: What is the Forsaken's New Plague?
faq.answer: The Royal Apothecary Society developed the New Plague in the Undercity. This chemical and magical pathogen is designed to kill both living mortals and the Lich King's undead thralls.

angles.text: The Plague of Undeath destroyed the Kingdom of Lordaeron and tore families apart. Its devastation became humanity's greatest historical catastrophe.
Many Forsaken bear the plague's physical scars. They endured its agony, died, and later broke free of the Lich King's psychic grip.
The Order of the Silver Hand shattered while trying to contain the contagion. Paladins now rely on the Holy Light to purge its foul residue.
Priests face the plague's corruption of body and spirit. Their faith drives them to burn away necrotic sickness before it festers.
The loss of the northern kingdoms to the plague remains an unhealed wound for the Alliance. It drives the Alliance's ongoing crusade to cleanse the Plaguelands.
Orcs and tauren viewed the northern sickness as a human curse. The Royal Apothecary Society's research has since brought the horror of plague experimentation into the Horde.
